info.title: Strava Login App API
info.description: Sign in with Strava, then read your profile. Requests are authenticated with the better-auth session cookie, so 'Try it out' works from a browser that is already signed in. The auth endpoints themselves (/api/auth/*) are documented separately at /api/auth/reference.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: The signed-in athlete's runs and their streams

tags.name: Coach
tags.description: Conversations with the AI running coach

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Strava push subscription callbacks — called by Strava, not the browser

tags.name: Telemetry
tags.description: Browser events and errors, forwarded to Loki

sessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
sessionCookie.description: Set by better-auth after the Strava OAuth callback.

get.description: Reads the session, takes the stored Strava access token (refreshing it when expired), and proxies GET /athlete from the Strava API.

502.description: Strava rejected or failed the upstream request.

get.description: Proxies GET /athlete/activities from the Strava API and keeps only run-type activities (Run, TrailRun, VirtualRun).

200.description: The athlete's runs, most recent first.

403.description: The stored Strava token lacks the activity:read scope; sign out and back in.

502.description: Strava rejected or failed the upstream request.

get.summary: Get one run's GPS and sensor streams
get.description: Proxies GET /activities/{id}/streams from the Strava API. Activities without streams (e.g. manual entries) yield an empty object.

200.description: The run's streams, keyed by type.

403.description: The stored Strava token lacks the activity:read scope; sign out and back in.

502.description: Strava rejected or failed the upstream request.

get.description: Reads the persisted render state for this run and athlete. `render` is null when the run has never been rendered. While a render is in flight, live progress comes from the SSE endpoint, which also keeps this state up to date.

200.description: The stored render, or null if none exists.

post.summary: Render this run's video on Remotion Lambda
post.description: Fetches the run and its streams from Strava, starts a Remotion Lambda render of the story video, and persists the render state. The MP4 lands in the Remotion S3 bucket. Idempotent while a render is in flight or already done with the same options — those return the existing state; a failed render, or one whose options no longer match, is rendered again. The body is optional and defaults to the plain replay.

200.description: The render that is now in flight (or already finished).

403.description: The stored Strava token lacks the activity:read scope; sign out and back in.

502.description: Strava or Lambda failed the upstream request.

503.description: Remotion Lambda is not configured on this server, or rendering is switched off for this athlete by the `video-render` feature flag.

get.description: Server-sent events. While the run's render is in flight, polls Remotion Lambda every ~1.5s, persists the result, and emits the updated RunRender as a JSON message. The final message has status `done` or `error`, after which the stream closes; a lone `null` message means there is no render. Consumed with EventSource, not the generated client.

200.description: An event stream of RunRender JSON messages.

503.description: Remotion Lambda is not configured on this server.

get.description: Most recently used first. A thread with no messages has a null title.

post.description: Returns an empty thread. Its title is filled in from the first message the athlete sends to it.

get.description: The thread and its full transcript, oldest message first.

404.description: No such conversation for this athlete.

delete.description: Removes the thread and every message in it.

404.description: No such conversation for this athlete.

get.summary: The coach's read on the athlete, before they ask anything
get.description: Everything the Coach screen's rails show: the goal race the coach remembers, this week's accepted plan measured against what was actually run, the measured training signals (load ratio, easy-run intensity, aerobic decoupling, shoe mileage) and the queue of things worth asking about. Signals that cannot be computed from the athlete's data are omitted rather than returned empty.

403.description: The stored Strava token lacks the activity:read scope; sign out and back in.

502.description: Strava rejected or failed the upstream request.

put.summary: Change what the coach remembers between threads
put.description: Merges into the stored context. An omitted field is left alone; a field sent as null is cleared — that is the difference between changing the target time and dropping the race. The coach writes here too, through its setAthleteContext tool.

post.summary: Accept a week the coach proposed
post.description: Stores the seven sessions as the athlete's week and returns them measured against what they have already run. Accepting again for the same week replaces it, which is what a revision is.

200.description: The accepted week, against what was actually run.

403.description: The stored Strava token lacks the activity:read scope; sign out and back in.

502.description: Strava rejected or failed the upstream request.

post.summary: Send a message and stream the coach's reply
post.description: Loads the thread's transcript, appends the incoming message, and streams the model's answer as an AI SDK UI message stream — text, reasoning and tool calls as they happen. Both the athlete's message and the finished reply are persisted, so the browser never has to send the history back. Consumed by `useChat` from @ai-sdk/react, not by the generated client.

200.description: A UI message stream of the coach's reply.

400.description: The request named no message to answer.

404.description: No such conversation for this athlete.

503.description: No model API key is configured on this server.

get.description: Strava calls this while `POST /push_subscriptions` is in flight and expects `{ "hub.challenge": … }` back within two seconds. The challenge is only echoed when `hub.verify_token` matches the server's STRAVA_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN, so somebody else's subscription cannot point at this callback.

403.description: The verify token did not match, or none is configured.

post.summary: Receive a Strava activity or athlete event
post.description: Acknowledged immediately and processed afterwards: Strava requires a 200 within two seconds and retries up to three times otherwise, which is far less time than reading an activity and writing a debrief takes. A new run becomes a post-run debrief in the athlete's "Post-run debriefs" thread; everything else is recorded and ignored.

200.description: Acknowledged. Always, whatever the event turns out to be.

post.summary: Forward a batch of browser events
post.description: Re-logs events the browser recorded — user actions, failed requests, uncaught errors — through the server logger, so client and server lines share one stream in Loki. Deliberately open to signed-out callers: a crash on the sign-in page is exactly what this is for. The session, when there is one, only adds attribution.

202.description: The batch was accepted for logging.
